page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv4 family, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. It allocates 64 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 32 physical cores via two threads per core. System memory is configured at 256 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 48 MB of Level 3 cache along with instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI).

A key architectural component is the inclusion of 2,577 GB of local solid-state drive (SSD) storage bundled directly with the instance. In benchmark evaluations, the memory subsystem demonstrates high throughput, reaching 207.3 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations and 95.23 GB/sec in large-block write operations, placing memory bandwidth in the top tier. PassMark evaluations reflect similar strengths in database operations and extended CPU vector instruction tests, while multi-core computational tasks like stress-ng and Geekbench compiler workloads perform within expected median levels.

Without discrete hardware acceleration, the instance experiences limited throughput on large language model inference tasks, such as generating text with 70B parameter models. However, the balance of high vCPU density, 256 GB of memory, and fast local NVMe-based SSD capacity creates a cost-efficient profile for traditional enterprise backends without the expense of specialized GPU hardware. Appropriate workloads include relational database servers, high-concurrency static web serving, software build clusters, and data ingestion pipelines requiring rapid local caching.
description: The Microsoft Azure D64ds_v4 is a general-purpose cloud server configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz and 256 GB of system RAM. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 32 physical cores with multithreading, 48 MB of L3 cache, and AVX-512 extensions. The server includes 2,577 GB of bundled local SSD storage, avoiding pure reliance on remote volumes for high-throughput temporary data. Benchmark testing demonstrates strong performance in uncached memory read and write bandwidth as well as PassMark database operations, while general multi-core computing metrics align with average distribution levels. Lacking discrete GPUs, the instance is not suited for high-parameter LLM inference, but its balanced resource allocation offers cost efficiency for production database workloads, software compilation, ETL data pipelines, and scalable web serving.
